Calendar line 1 – Tentative Ruling
Case Name: THE ESTATE OF CORINNA TINOCO
Case Number: 23PR195554

INTRODUCTION
On August 29, 2023, Patricia Tinoco and Guadalupe Tinoco (“Petitioners”) filed a
petition for probate of the estate of their mother, Corinna Tinoco, in docket 23PR195554. On
January 20, 2026, Petitioners filed a motion to surcharge former successor trustee, Andrea
Padrone (“Padrone”). No opposition to the motion has been filed.

DISCUSSION
Petitioners argue that Padron, a former trustee of the Corinna Tinoco 2020 Revocable
Trust dated October 12, 2020, failed to provide a code-compliant accounting and failed to
provide information to the beneficiaries, resulting in Petitioners ultimately filing a petition, in
docket 23PR195174, to remove Padrone as trustee, to appoint Petitioners as co-trustees, for an
accounting, to surcharge Padrone, and for attorney fees and costs. Ultimately, on June 24,
2025, after Padrone failed to appear multiple times, the court (Hon. Lê Jacqueline Dương)
ordered Padrone to provide an accounting and ordered that she be surcharged in an amount
according to proof. The court issued its order after hearing in docket 23PR195174, on June 24,
2025.

Here, despite the court’s order surcharging Padrone according to proof, this court must
deny the motion for two reasons. First, the motion must be filed and noticed in the trust case,
The Corinna Tinoco 2020 Revocable Trust, docket 23PR195174. While the court might under
different circumstances be able to overlook this procedural issue, a different judge, the
Honorable Charles Adams in Department 7, is presiding over the trust case, which remains
active. Notably, the minute order from December 12, 2025 in docket 23PR195174 indicates
that a hearing is scheduled for March 25, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. in Department 7 “pending
surcharge petition.”1
Second, and more fundamentally, while Petitioners have filed a notice of hearing
noticing the instant motion, the proof of service does not indicate who was served. No
additional proof of service has been filed and the time in which to file same has passed. (See
Cal. Rules of Court, rule 3.1300(c) [“Proof of service of the moving papers must be filed no
later than five court days before the time appointed for the hearing.”].) Thus, Petitioners have
not established that they have served Padrone or her counsel of record with the instant motion.
Notably, no opposition has been filed, potentially suggesting that Padrone or her counsel were
not served.

The motion is DENIED WITHOUT PREJUDICE to refiling in the correct docket number with
appropriate service.
1 No surcharge petition was filed in docket 23PR195174.
